title: The Awareness Campaign
summary: We read a magazine editorial about diet, lifestyle and health problems. We learned phrases for 'too much' and 'too little' and expressions for cause and effect, like 'lead to' and 'be caused by'. Then we held a meeting to agree on two topics for a school health awareness campaign.

grammar.title: Talking about 'too much' and 'too little'
grammar.explain: We use special phrases to say there is too much or too little of something. For too much: a surplus of, an excessive amount of, high in. For too little: a lack of, a shortage of, an absence of, insufficient, not enough, low in, poor in, lacking in.
grammar.explain_ar: نستخدم عبارات خاصة لنقول إن هناك كمية زائدة أو ناقصة من شيء ما. للكثرة الزائدة: a surplus of وan excessive amount of وhigh in. وللنقص: a lack of وa shortage of وan absence of وinsufficient وnot enough وlow in وpoor in وlacking in.
form: Too much (M): a surplus of / an excessive amount of + uncountable noun; an excessive number of + plural noun
Too much (M): be + high in + noun (This food is high in salt.)
Too little (L): a lack of / a shortage of / an absence of + noun
Too little (L): insufficient / not enough + noun (insufficient sleep, not enough exercise)
Too little (L): be + low in / poor in / lacking in + noun (low in vitamins)

examples.en: Not having enough relaxation time can lead to stress-related disorders.
Dizziness may be caused by insufficient fresh air.
Convenience foods can be low in nutritional value.
A lot of fast food contains an excessive amount of sugar.
examples.note: amount of + uncountable noun (sugar) = too much

examples.en: Some people's dietary habits show an absence of fruit and vegetables.
examples.note: an absence of = none or too little

examples.en: A lack of time can make people feel out of control and anxious.
examples.note: a lack of + noun = too little

mistakes.wrong: Fast food has an excessive number of sugar.
mistakes.right: Fast food has an excessive amount of sugar.
mistakes.why: Sugar is uncountable, so use 'amount of'. Use 'number of' with plural nouns.

mistakes.wrong: This soup is high of salt.
mistakes.right: This soup is high in salt.
mistakes.why: The preposition is 'in': high in, low in, poor in, lacking in.

mistakes.wrong: There is a lack in time.
mistakes.right: There is a lack of time.
mistakes.why: The noun 'lack' takes 'of'. The adjective 'lacking' takes 'in'.

mistakes.wrong: Too much salt and sugars are bad for you.
mistakes.right: Too much salt and sugar is bad for you.
mistakes.why: Sugar is uncountable here, so don't add -s.

mistakes.wrong: Many people are having a serious health problems.
mistakes.right: Many people are having serious health problems.
mistakes.why: Don't use 'a' with a plural noun.

quiz.q: Children who eat only sweets have a ___ vitamins.
quiz.why: Too little: a lack of + noun.

quiz.q: Fizzy drinks contain an excessive ___ of sugar.

quiz.why: A surplus is more than you need.

quiz.q: Many teenagers get ___ sleep because they use their phones at night.
quiz.why: The meaning is too little sleep: insufficient.

quiz.q: His diet is lacking ___ fresh vegetables.

grammar.title: Cause and effect expressions
grammar.explain: We use these expressions to connect a cause with its result. Put the cause first with lead to, contribute to, cause or bring on. Put the result first with be caused by, be provoked by or be aggravated by.
grammar.explain_ar: نستخدم هذه التعبيرات لربط السبب بنتيجته. نضع السبب أولاً مع lead to وcontribute to وcause وbring on. ونضع النتيجة أولاً مع الصيغ المبنية للمجهول be caused by وbe provoked by وbe aggravated by.
form: Cause + (can) lead to / contribute(s) to + result (noun or -ing)
Result + is / can be caused by / provoked by / aggravated (further) by + cause
..., causing + someone + to + verb (adds a result at the end of a sentence)

examples.en: Undoubtedly smoking can lead to an increased threat of developing lung cancer.
Existing skin allergies can sometimes be aggravated further by suntan lotion.
examples.note: result + be aggravated by + cause (made worse)

examples.en: Physical exercise can bring on a sense of emotional well-being.
Many parents work long hours, causing them to rely on convenience food.
Insomnia can be provoked by too much stress and a lack of physical exercise.
Consuming excessive amounts of sweet fizzy drinks contributes to tooth decay.

mistakes.wrong: Smoking can lead to have lung cancer.
mistakes.right: Smoking can lead to lung cancer.
mistakes.why: 'To' in 'lead to' is a preposition: use a noun or -ing after it, not a base verb.

mistakes.wrong: Insomnia can be provoked from stress.
mistakes.right: Insomnia can be provoked by stress.
mistakes.why: In the passive, use 'by' before the cause.

mistakes.wrong: Too much sugar causes to weight gain.
mistakes.right: Too much sugar causes weight gain.
mistakes.why: 'Cause' takes a direct object, with no 'to'.

mistakes.wrong: If you have a stress, you can't sleep good.
mistakes.right: If you have stress, you can't sleep well.
mistakes.why: 'Stress' is uncountable here, and we use the adverb 'well' after a verb.

quiz.q: Eating too much salt can ___ high blood pressure.
quiz.why: The cause comes first, so use 'lead to'.

quiz.q: Tooth decay is often ___ too much sugar.
quiz.why: The result comes first, so use the passive 'caused by'.

quiz.q: Long hours at a desk can ___ back pain.
Her asthma was aggravated further ___ the smoke.
The trains were late, ___ many people to miss work.
quiz.why: '..., causing + someone + to + verb' adds a result.

quiz.q: A lack of sleep ___ poor concentration at school.

grammar.title: Making suggestions in a meeting
grammar.explain: In the meeting we suggested ideas for the awareness campaign. After 'What about' and 'How about', use the -ing form. After 'Why don't we', 'Let's' and 'We should', use the base verb.
grammar.explain_ar: في الاجتماع اقترحنا أفكاراً لحملة التوعية. بعد What about وHow about نستخدم الفعل مع ing. وبعد Why don't we وLet's وWe should نستخدم الفعل في صيغته الأساسية.
form: I think we should + base verb ...

examples.en: What about focusing on healthy eating?
How about teaching kids the difference between healthy and unhealthy food?
Why don't we invite a doctor to talk to the students?
Let's choose lack of sleep and sedentary lifestyles.
I think we should protect children from stress at school.
examples.note: should + base verb; protect someone from something

mistakes.wrong: What about to collect money for the campaign?
mistakes.right: What about collecting money for the campaign?

mistakes.wrong: We want to learn the kids the difference.
mistakes.right: We want to teach the kids the difference.
mistakes.why: You teach someone something; you learn something yourself.

mistakes.wrong: We need to prevent them from stress.
mistakes.right: We need to protect them from stress.
mistakes.why: Protect someone from something. 'Prevent' needs an action: prevent them from getting stressed.
After 'Let's' use the base verb without 'to'.

quiz.q: What about ___ a poster about sugar?
Why don't we ___ on sleep and stress?
We want to ___ children how to read food labels.
Sun cream can ___ your skin from the sun.
Let's ___ two topics for the campaign.

phrases.en: I think ... should get priority because ...
phrases.use: Giving your opinion with a reason

phrases.en: This can lead to serious problems like ...
I see what you mean, but ...
Before we decide, let's discuss all the options.
It's not too late to turn the tide.

phrases.use: Ending on a positive note (from the editorial)
